significance: A coastal Divya Desam on the Mahabalipuram road whose original structure was raised by the 7th-century Pallavas with 11th-century Chola additions. Its sanctum holds a rare seven-foot granite Varaha bearing Bhudevi on his lap, and the shrine is favoured by those seeking marriage.
story: Varaha is said to have wedded the 360 daughters of the sage Kalava one on each day of the year, becoming the 'ever-marrying' Nithyakalyana Perumal.
